newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end lower after French poll.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end lower after French poll.

text.p: Milan shares closed easier on Monday at around the day's lows following the decline in French stocks after the surprise lead of left wing parties shown in the first round of French parliamentary elections on Sunday.

With Britain and U.S. closed for a market holiday, Milan stocks chose to focus on the French poll which showed the combined left having a lead over the centre-right, and so increased uncertainties over Europe's single currency going ahead on time, they added.
The all-share Mibtel index ended off 1.43 percent at 12,253 while the Mib30 closed down 1.6 percent at 18,248.
Despite firmer domestic bonds, Italian stocks had little enthusiasm to push forward and most of the major blue chip stocks fell back in line with the overall market.

One to stand out was banking stock San Paolo, up 0.78 percent at 10,785 lire after its share offering closed on Friday with the new share issue priced for the public at 10,435 lire a share and for institutional investors at 10,630 lire.

Fiat minimised losses, down 0.69 percent at 5,433 lire after its chairman Cesare Romiti said in a newspaper interview that its 1997 sales would be around 90 trillion lire and its profits in 1997 would not be less than 1996.
Analysts said that Romiti's comments showed that Fiat's sales were gaining from Italy's new car incentive scheme and that operating profits were starting to improve.

Shares in Banca Commerciale Italiana (BCI) continued to suffer on talks it maybe on the takeover trail with its shares off 2.75 percent at 3,355 lire. But talk of BCI taking over Banca di Roma on Friday had faded by Monday and the shares of the Rome-based bank were off 2.16 percent at 1,266 lire.
